payload.summary: The Codex auto-resolve workflow reversed an explicit owner decision on a clinical surface without approval, and no gate distinguishes a bot finding from a decision already made
payload.detail: OBSERVED 2026-08-22/23 on PR #2314 (branch claude/form-pages-structure-kaboq6, merged as 1ed7753). WHAT HAPPENED: the owner was asked, and chose, to display drafted (not yet clinician-reviewed) Mental Health Act section summaries on the Forms pages WITH a visible 'awaiting clinical review' warning label, rather than hiding them until sign-off. That decision was implemented, and the reasoning was recorded in docs/wiring-conventions.md. A Codex review then raised the opposite as a P1 finding, and .github/workflows/codex-autofix-review-comments.yml dispatched the automatic repair pass, which applied it. THE EFFECT WAS NOT A NARROW EDIT: the fix inverted the render gate in src/lib/mha-act-sections.ts to status !== 'reviewed' AND hardcoded reviewStatus: 'reviewed' on every emitted section, so the Act-sections card collapsed from 54 forms to 1 while every surviving summary lost its awaiting-review caveat. A SECOND, INDEPENDENT GATE on the same predicate had also been introduced in supplementalCueByCode; after removing the obvious one the count measured 47/54, not 54/54, and only a direct recount caught it. Both were removed and the state restored before merge; the merged tree is verified at 54/54 by direct count. THE STANDING RISK, which is what this row is for: (1) The workflow's routing rules (AGENTS.md 'Automatic resolve trigger') gate on PATH RISK and DIFF SIZE - migrations, API routes, auth, clinical/RAG paths, >=10 files or >=300 lines - and this diff qualified as high-risk, which ROUTED it rather than held it. There is no rule anywhere that says a finding contradicting a decision the owner already made must go back to the owner instead of being auto-applied, and no mechanism by which the workflow could know a decision exists. (2) 'Always fix P0 and P1 findings' is unconditional in AGENTS.md, so a bot's severity label alone is sufficient authority to overwrite a human choice. (3) The bot's own comment reported the change as 'Fixed'; the reversal was found only by reading the merged code and counting, not by trusting that report - the third-party-fix-claim rule in AGENTS.md is what caught it. (4) The rationale for the owner's decision WAS written down, in docs/wiring-conventions.md, and that was not enough - nothing consults it. OPTIONS FOR THE OWNER TO DECIDE BETWEEN, none implemented: (a) exclude clinical-output surfaces (src/lib/mha-act-sections.ts, form-catalog, forms components, data/mha-2014-sections.json) from automatic repair entirely, so those findings are always reported to a human; (b) require an explicit human ack before the automatic pass touches any file whose diff also changes a rendering/eligibility GATE rather than its content; (c) treat the skip-codex-review label as the standing control and apply it by default to clinical PRs. NEXT: pick one and encode it in .github/workflows/codex-autofix-review-comments.yml plus its AGENTS.md contract. STOP: do not treat this as closed because #2314's specific regression was repaired - the repair was manual and reactive, and the same sequence would recur on the next clinical PR. SIBLING: #JZM7RM records two auto-fixers racing on ONE comment; this row is the different failure of one governed auto-fixer applying a finding it had no way to know was already decided against.
